QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_54

question.text: When a fixed-coupon bond trades at a premium to its face value (price > face value), its Yield to Maturity (YTM) is:

explanation.text: The Logic: YTM is the internal rate of return that equates the discounted present value of a bond's future coupon and principal cash flows with its current price. If a bond's price is above face value, the holder effectively pays more than they will receive at redemption, so the realised yield (YTM) is lower than the stated coupon rate. The general relationship: price < face → YTM > coupon; price = face → YTM = coupon; price > face → YTM < coupon. The Trap: "Equal to coupon" applies only when price = face; "greater than coupon" applies to discount bonds; "zero" is mathematically inconsistent with a positive coupon and positive face value at maturity. Note: The XIX-A workbook defines YTM as the FIRR of a fixed-tenor debt investment held to maturity and provides the present-value cash-flow equation; it does not explicitly state the premium/discount/par YTM-coupon relationship. Treat that relationship as general fixed-income theory.
